items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: and then the big one for me, Bobby McFerrin, of course not a sax player, a vocalist. But hearing him perform and just one guy, no electronics, no looping, one guy on the stage

ctx.x: would I listen to that and so when was the first time you tried that by yourself in front of an audience?

Oh yeah, yeah. Well a cool thing is that I was able to do it online first in the sense of posting a YouTube video. Yes I had experimented a little bit before. I was teaching down in Texas, Abeline Christian University, I was a full time instructor for six years. And that time was really good for me. So I did undergrad, Hope College; graduate school University of Cincinnati. And when you’re a student you’re learning so, so much. But there’s also this kind of underwritten kind of competition. There’s this intensity…

amazing stuff you’ve ever heard, and the most creative stuff, and just being like I want to be able to do that but on the saxophone. And so then slowly over the years progressing and adding — oh wonder if I could get — I had this pop sound, I wonder if I could kind of get a hi-hat sound, and then thinking, also thinking of other instruments I’ve explored. I’ve played drumset a little bit and thinking okay so where’s my bass drum sound? Where’s my snare? Okay could I do like a roll sound? And then okay I have a…
